bnqa25:353: The deepest insight of the five-layer cost methodology is the one-way dependency between layers: the bottom layer (usage habits) yields the highest returns but has the lowest ceiling, while the top layer (Agent architecture) demands the largest upfront investment but delivers continuous marginal returns. A common mistake is skipping the bottom layers and going straight to architecture refactoring—if a single Session mixes multiple tasks or compact is never used, context bloat can multiply and devour the gains from upper-layer architectural optimization. Thus "usage habits → model routing → context engineering → code graph → Agent architecture" is both an implementation order and an ROI ranking: each step up addresses structural waste that the lower layers cannot reach. Subagent isolation deserves special caution—it looks like "offloading the burden to sub-agents," but in reality it is independently billed context.
